replication.target_description: Study 2: independent high-anchor Studio 97 versus low-anchor Studio 17 comparison of restaurant meal price estimates, Table 2, primary outlier-excluded analysis.

n.location: p.6, Table 2, Restaurant row, High n and Low n columns
n.sample_role: Participants contributing one restaurant estimate each to the independent two-group test; sum of mutually exclusive final High and Low anchor groups.
n.exclusions: Same item-specific 1.5 IQR outlier rule as Study 1; p.6 reports 7.37% across observations, and two ambiguous estimates treated as missing, without assigning those two to the restaurant item. Recruitment N=273 is not used as analytic N.

p.location: p.6, Table 2, Restaurant row, High n and Low n columns; p.6, Study 2 Results

reported_success.quote: Participants did not estimate ... that a meal at Studio 97 would be more expensive than ... one at Studio 17

notes: Identity independently confirmed from title page and closing citation: Shanks, Barbieri-Hermitte and Vadillo (2020), Do Incidental Environmental Anchors Bias Consumers’ Price Estimations?, Collabra: Psychology 6(1):19, DOI 10.1525/collabra.310; labelled ORIGINAL RESEARCH REPORT. Supplied canonical text contains all 15 article pages, methods, results, tables and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendered. Target selected by supplied study identifier, restaurant outcome, and the article’s explicit connection to Critcher and Gilovich Study 3 and Dogerlioglu-Demir and Koçaş Study 1 (p.3 Study 1 aims, p.5 discussion, p.7 Study 3). Business-name wording is interpreted in that explicit original-study context as Studio 97 versus Studio 17, rather than Tap 92 versus Tap 42. Repeated indistinguishable locators receive the same source-supported restaurant test; no assignment by row order or numeric matching. Study 2 locator p.5 introduces its restaurant design; its results are on p.6. Analytic N derivation: 127 + 125 = 252. High and Low are exclusive randomized anchor conditions for the same restaurant item, not repeated observations to be pooled across items. Table 2 Restaurant: Cohen’s d 0.01, t 0.07, df 250, BF+0 0.15. No numerical restaurant p or numerical p bound is printed. Do not compute p from t or reinterpret BF+0 as p. Unassigned original and effect-size fields are placeholders only.
